data.gender_notes: Ramprawesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ram means God and Prawesh means abundance and power. This name signifies the god of abundance and power. The name Ramprawesh carries the meaning “God of Abundance and Power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Ramprawesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god of abundance and power and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Ramprawesh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Abundance and Power.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ramprawesh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ramprawesh has deep cultural roots in Hinduism, where the name Ram is a revered name for God, indicating the divine aspect of the being. The name Prawesh signifies power and abundance, associated with the Hindu gods of wealth and prosperity, such as Lakshmi and Ganesha. This name reflects the Hindu belief in the divine powers that bring prosperity and wealth.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ramprawesh holds great spiritual significance for Hindus. The name Ram is a reminder of their devotion to God and their belief in the eternal presence of the divine. The name Prawesh signifies the divine power of the universe that bestows abundance and prosperity upon those who seek it with pure hearts and minds. Thus, the name Ramprawesh serves as a call to connect with the divine power for spiritual growth and material abundance.

historical_references.reference: Rampal, a descendant of Raja Dhruva Rao, was the last independent king of Vijayanagara Empire in 1565. He is also known as Rampal Raya or Rampreetha Raya. After his death, the Vijayanagara Empire was ruled by the Sultanate of Bijapur and the Kingdom of Mysore.

Rampal Verma, a king of the Agrawal Rajput clan, is mentioned in the historical text 'Ain-i-Akbari' written by Abul Fazl around 1590. He is described as the king of the region around the town of Raisen in present-day Madhya Pradesh, India.
